author: The Church of Smyrna
addressee: The church of God that sojourns at Philomelium and all communities of the holy and catholic church
occasion: The church of Smyrna writes to report the martyrdom of Polycarp and other martyrs, and to present Polycarp's death as a model of martyrdom according to the gospel.
argument: The letter reports that recent martyrs endured tortures with remarkable courage, and that Polycarp, after a vision foretelling his death by fire, was arrested and brought before the proconsul. Polycarp refused to swear by Caesar's fortune or revile Christ, confessing himself a Christian and rejecting the proconsul's threats. Condemned to be burned, he prayed a long prayer of praise and was killed by a dagger when the fire miraculously failed to consume him. The church collected his bones and resolved to commemorate his martyrdom annually, presenting him as a model for imitation.

outline.move: The church of Smyrna greets the church of Philomelium and all catholic communities.
The writers explain that Polycarp's martyrdom sealed the persecution and that his surrender imitated the Lord's example.
The courage of the martyrs under torture is described, including their endurance of fire and beasts.
Germanicus's brave death stirs the crowd to demand the arrest of Polycarp.
Quintus, who volunteered but then sacrificed, is cited as a warning against self-surrender.
Polycarp withdraws to a farm and has a vision of his pillow burning, foretelling his death by fire.

Polycarp moves to another farm, but a tortured slave betrays him, and Herod the eirenarch seeks to bring him to the stadium so that Polycarp may fulfill his allotted lot as a partaker of Christ, while his betrayers would receive Judas's punishment.
Polycarp is found, feeds his captors, and prays for two hours before being taken to the city.
Herod and Nicetes urge Polycarp to say 'Lord Caesar' and sacrifice, but he refuses and is taken to the stadium.
A heavenly voice encourages Polycarp; before the proconsul he refuses to swear by Caesar's fortune or revile Christ.
Polycarp confesses he is a Christian and declines to defend himself before the crowd.
Polycarp dismisses the proconsul's threats of beasts and fire, speaking of the eternal fire awaiting the wicked.
The herald announces Polycarp's confession; the crowd demands he be burned alive.
The crowd gathers wood; Polycarp removes his clothes and refuses to be nailed to the pyre.
Polycarp is bound and prays a long prayer of praise and thanksgiving to God.
The fire is lit but forms an arch around Polycarp, leaving him like baking bread or refined metal, with a fragrant smell.
A confector stabs Polycarp with a dagger, and a dove and a great quantity of blood come out, extinguishing the fire; the writer praises Polycarp as an apostolic and prophetic teacher.

The devil prompts Nicetes to petition the magistrate not to give the body, saying 'lest they abandon the crucified one and begin to worship this man,' and the Jews join in suggesting and supporting this; the writer explains the proper honor due to martyrs.
The centurion burns the body; the Christians collect the bones and plan to celebrate the anniversary of his martyrdom.
Polycarp is remembered as the twelfth martyr in Smyrna and an outstanding teacher and witness.
The letter is sent via Marcianus, with a closing doxology and greetings.
The date and circumstances of Polycarp's martyrdom are recorded.
A closing blessing and a note on the manuscript's transmission through Gaius, Socrates, and Pionius.
An alternative transmission note adds details about Irenaeus, Marcion, and a voice heard in Rome at Polycarp's death, and names the copyists Gaius, Isocrates, and Pionius.

cast.name: Polycarp
cast.who: Bishop of the church in Smyrna and the central martyr of the letter.

cast.name: Germanicus
cast.who: A courageous martyr who fought wild beasts and inspired the crowd.

cast.name: Quintus
cast.who: A Phrygian who volunteered for martyrdom but sacrificed under pressure.

cast.name: Herod
cast.who: The eirenarch (police captain) who arrested Polycarp.

cast.name: Nicetes
cast.who: Herod's father, who urged Polycarp to sacrifice and later tried to prevent the recovery of his body.

cast.name: Philip
cast.who: The Asiarch who refused to release a lion against Polycarp.

cast.name: Marcianus
cast.who: Our brother through whom the letter was communicated.

cast.name: Evaristus
cast.who: The one who wrote the letter with his whole household; possibly the amanuensis.

cast.name: Gaius
cast.who: A copyist in the manuscript tradition.

cast.name: Socrates
cast.who: A copyist in Corinth who wrote from Gaius's copies.

cast.name: Isocrates
cast.who: A copyist in Corinth named in the alternative epilogue.

cast.name: Pionius
cast.who: The final copyist who recovered and transcribed the text.

cast.name: Irenaeus
cast.who: A disciple of Polycarp whose writings preserved the martyrdom account.

cast.name: Marcion
cast.who: The heretic whom Polycarp called the firstborn of Satan.

scripture: The author uses Septuagint book names and Psalm numbering. Citations should be given in modern form, e.g. LXX Psalm numbering converted to Hebrew/English numbering where they differ.
uncertain: The exact year of Polycarp's death; the date given in section 21 is debated.
The identity of the 'great Sabbath' and its relation to the Passover dating.
The precise role and title of the 'confector' in section 16.
The relationship between the two epilogues and the original ending of the letter.
The discrepancy between the copyist names Socrates (section 22) and Isocrates (epilogus_alius).

_unresolved_facts.claim: Statius Quadratus ... The proconsul who tried Polycarp.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: συνελήφθη δὲ ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου ἐπὶ ἀρχιερέως Φιλίππου Τραλλιανοῦ, ἀνθυπατεύοντος Στατίου Κοδράτου
_unresolved_facts.fix: Statius Quadratus is named as the proconsul (ἀνθυπατεύοντος) under whom Polycarp was arrested, but the text does not say he personally tried Polycarp; the one who interrogates Polycarp is consistently called 'ὁ ἀνθύπατος' (the proconsul) without being named.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Marcianus ... Our brother through whom the letter was communicated.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἡμεῖς δὲ κατὰ τὸ παρὸν ἐπὶ κεφαλαίῳ μεμηνύκαμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ἡμῶν Μαρκίωνος
_unresolved_facts.fix: Marcion (Μαρκίωνος), not Marcianus. The brief misspells the name.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Evaristus ... The one who wrote the letter with his whole household; possibly the amanuensis.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἡμῖν προσαγορεύουσιν καὶ Εὐάρεστος ὁ γράψας πανοικεί
_unresolved_facts.fix: Evaristus is named as 'ὁ γράψας πανοικεί' (the one who wrote with his whole household), but 'wrote' here likely means 'wrote greetings' or 'sent greetings' with his household, not that he was the amanuensis who composed the letter.

Polycarp does not speak in section 5; the vision is narrated about him ('εἶδεν... καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν' is narration of his words to companions, but section 5 contains no direct speech marked with quotation). He speaks in sections 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14. In epilogus_alius, it is Marcion who speaks to Polycarp, not Polycarp initiating speech.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Irenaeus ... Cited as source for quotations in the epilogue
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ταῦτα μετεγράψατο μὲν Γάϊος ἐκ τῶν Εἰρηναίου συγγραμμάτων... λέγει δὲ καὶ τοῦτο... καὶ τοῦτο δὲ φέρεται ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Εἰρηναίου συγγράμμασιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Irenaeus is cited as the source from which Gaius copied, and his writings are said to contain certain information, but Irenaeus is not directly quoted speaking; the epilogue narrates about Irenaeus's writings and what they contained.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Marcion ... Direct speech quoted in the epilogue
_unresolved_facts.fix: Marcion speaks in the epilogue, but the brief has the wrong Marcion: it should be Marcion the heretic (Μαρκίωνος), not Marcianus. Also, the brief's cast list conflates two different people named Μαρκίωνος: the brother Marcion in section 20 and the heretic Marcion in epilogus_alius.

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["6"], move: '...Herod the eirenarch seeks to bring him to the stadium so that Polycarp may fulfill his allotted lot as a partaker of Christ, while his betrayers would receive Judas's punishment.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁ εἰρήναρχος, ὁ κεκληρωμένος τὸ αὐτὸ ὄνομα, Ἡρώδης ἐπιλεγόμενος, ἔσπευδεν εἰς τὸ στάδιον αὐτὸν εἰσαγαγεῖν, ἵνα ἐκεῖνος μὲν τὸν ἴδιον κλῆρον ἀπαρτίσῃ Χριστοῦ κοινωνὸς γενόμενος, οἱ δὲ προδόντες αὐτὸν τὴν αὐτοῦ τοῦ Ἰούδα ὑπόσχοιεν τιμωρίαν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The eirenarch is 'Herodes' (Ἡρώδης), called 'the one having obtained the same name' (ὁ κεκληρωμένος τὸ αὐτὸ ὄνομα)—meaning he shares the name with Herod the Great or another Herod. The brief's cast entry correctly notes 'Herod' but the outline move should clarify this is the eirenarch Herod, not that 'Herod the eirenarch' is a full title.

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["17"], move: 'The devil prompts Nicetes to petition the magistrate not to give the body, saying 'lest they abandon the crucified one and begin to worship this man,' and the Jews join in suggesting and supporting this...'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὑπέβαλεν γοῦν Νικήτην τὸν τοῦ Ἡρώδου πατέρα, ἀδελφὸν δὲ Ἄλκης, ἐντυχεῖν τῷ ἄρχοντι... καὶ ταῦτα εἶπον ὑποβαλλόντων καὶ ἐνισχυόντων τῶν Ἰουδαίων
_unresolved_facts.fix: The devil (ὁ ἀντίζηλος... ὁ ἀντικείμενος) prompted Nicetes, but the direct quote 'lest they abandon the crucified one and begin to worship this man' (μή, φησίν, ἀφέντες τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον τοῦτον ἄρξωνται σέβεσθαι) is what Nicetes said to the magistrate, not what the devil said. The Jews 'suggested and supported' (ὑποβαλλόντων καὶ ἐνισχυόντων) this—meaning they were the ones suggesting and strengthening the petition, not merely joining in. The brief reverses the agency: the devil prompted Nicetes, but the Jews were the ones suggesting and supporting.

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["epilogus_alius"], move: 'An alternative transmission note adds details about Irenaeus, Marcion, and a voice heard in Rome at Polycarp's death, and names the copyists Gaius, Isocrates, and Pionius.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐγὼ δὲ πάλιν Πιόνιος ἐκ τῶν Ἰσοκράτους ἀντιγράφων ἔγραψα
_unresolved_facts.fix: The epilogus_alius names Isocrates (Ἰσοκράτης), not 'Isocrates' as a variant of Socrates. But more importantly, the brief's cast list has Socrates in section 22 and Isocrates in epilogus_alius as different people, which is correct. However, the outline move says 'names the copyists Gaius, Isocrates, and Pionius'—but Gaius is not named as a copyist in epilogus_alius in the same way; the epilogue says Gaius transcribed from Irenaeus's writings (μετεγράψατο), and Isocrates wrote from Gaius's copies (ἔγραψα), and Pionius wrote from Isocrates's copies. The chain is Gaius → Isocrates → Pionius, not that all three are parallel copyists.
